hypothesis: Pre-convert K and V from bf16 to fp16 once per prefill call with a small streaming Triton kernel (_kv_to_fp16, writes contiguous fp16 [B, Skv, Hkv, D] workspace tensors from torch.empty), and feed those to the autotuned prefill _attn_fwd, so its in-loop k.to(fp16)/v.to(fp16) become no-ops and the fp16 tiles go straight from cp.async smem stages to ldmatrix/mma. Decode/split path and the small-Sq path are unchanged.
rationale: Since exps 12/13 both prefill mmas are fp16-accumulate, which forces a bf16->fp16 conversion of every K and V tile inside the inner loop. Triton applies it after the smem load in dot-operand layout, so every warp converts the whole 64x128 K tile and the whole V tile each iteration (~512 cvts per thread per iteration, 8x duplicated across the warps of a CTA, and repeated by every m-block and every one of the 32 q-heads that touches the tile). With mma now at 2x rate, this ALU/cvt work and its register pressure (HEAD prefill_16384: 255 regs, SM throughput 64%) compete with softmax for issue slots. A single conversion pass costs one read+write of K/V (8 MB at 2048, 134 MB at 32k: ~5-170 us, <=3% of prefill_2048 and ~0.5% of prefill_32768), and the converted tensors stay L2-resident for small prefills. Not tried before; exps 12-14 only changed the mma dtypes and tile list.
expected_effect: Prefill rows faster by ~3-10% on 4096-32768 (biggest on the thinnest prefill_32768/16384 margins), prefill_2048 roughly neutral (pre-pass cost vs loop savings), decode unchanged. Numerics identical to HEAD (same bf16->fp16 rounding, just done earlier).
